{{Short description|Belgian physicist}}
'''Constantin Piron''' (1932, Paris - 9 May 2012, [[Lausanne]]) was a Belgian physicist<ref>
{{cite journal
 |doi=10.1007/BF02057858
|bibcode = 1994FoPh...24.1107A
 |title=Constantin Piron at sixty-plus: Continuing a quest for the understanding of fundamental physical theories and the pursuit of their elaboration
 |year=1994
 |last1=Aerts
 |first1=Diederik
 |journal=Foundations of Physics
 |volume=24
 |issue=8
 |pages=1107–1111 }}</ref> who worked for most of his career in Switzerland.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://takingupspacetime.wordpress.com/2012/05/15/in-memoriam-constantin-piron/ |title=In Memoriam: Constantin Piron &#124; Taking up Spacetime |publisher=Takingupspacetime.wordpress.com |date= 16 May 2012|accessdate=2012-07-12}}</ref>
 
In 1963 Piron earned his doctor of science degree from the [[University of Lausanne]] under the direction of [[Ernst Stueckelberg]] and [[Josef-Maria Jauch]] with a thesis on [[quantum logic]], "Axiomatique quantique". He developed Jauch's methods (called the Geneva approach) for the foundations of [[quantum mechanics]].

Piron's theorem (1964)<ref>{{cite journal|author=Piron, C.|title=Axiomatique Quantique|journal=[[Helvetica Physica Acta]]|year=1964|volume=37|pages=439–468}}</ref> is a famous representation theorem for quantum lattices.{{cn|date=September 2025}}

He was appointed assistant professor in the physics department of the [[University of Geneva]] in 1969 and professor ordinarius in 1974. He retired in 2000.

Benjamin Inc., Massachusetts, 1976
*''Mécanique quantique: bases et applications'', [[Presses polytechniques et universitaires romandes]], 1990
*''Méthodes quantiques : Champs, N-corps, diffusion'', [[Presses polytechniques et universitaires romandes]].
